races.name: Zyn In-The-Moment Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Zyn Pacesetter British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Superior Choice
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good at Leopardstown last time, giving it the strongest form-fit for this trip and going; John & Thady Gosden yard in solid 14-day form (7/47); 55 days off the track but the stable handles that well, and the position at the head of affairs with no pressure is a significant tactical gift.

runners_data.name: Act Of Generosity
runners_data.note: Roger Varian sends this Roger Charlton-bred hold-up type here after a 55-day break; sole run showed a fifth over 10f on good, and the style demands a strong pace to exploit — the likely modest fractions set by an uncontested Superior Choice represent a real tactical obstacle.

runners_data.name: Hatteen
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's lightly-weighted runner (OR 82) has placed twice over 10f on good ground, showing the trip suits; a genuine rear-of-field operator by nature, it fills a midfield slot on the map only because the hold-up berths are occupied, so treat its mapped position with caution when assessing how much ground it will give away early.

runners_data.name: Ragazzo Grandi
runners_data.note: The critical unknown in this field — unraced or lightly-raced enough that style is unclassified, trainer Hilal Kobeissi has a modest 0-from-3 14-day strike rate, and the lack of form data means it could either slot prominently or race greenly; any positive signs in the paddock or early strides make it a significant variable.

runners_data.name: Zurna
runners_data.note: Julia & Shelley Birkett's filly ran seventh and ninth on soft ground over 10f, making the step up to good ground here a potential plus; back after only 11 days, and as a confirmed hold-up type she needs a gallop that stretches the field — not the shape this race is likely to produce.

races.paceDynamic: Superior Choice is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, will control fractions from the outset over 1m2f on good ground at Newmarket's July course. With Act Of Generosity, Hatteen, and Zurna all natural hold-up types, and Ragazzo Grandi's style unknown, Superior Choice can dictate a measured, uncontested gallop that suits a horse able to quicken off a sustainable pace. The redistribution note is relevant here: Hatteen is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield simply because there is no competition for that rear position, not because it will race prominently. This race shape — a lone leader controlling pace, likely modest fractions, with rivals needing to travel smoothly before producing a late effort — favours a prominent or mid-division horse with a sharp finishing kick over this mile-and-two-furlong trip; pure hold-up horses reliant on a strong pace to aim at are at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Superior Choice dictates a steady uncontested gallop and kicks clear in the final two furlongs before hold-up horses get organised.
scenarios.body: If Superior Choice dictates a steady uncontested gallop and kicks clear in the final two furlongs before hold-up horses get organised.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to bring hold-up horses into the race late and Superior Choice ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fast enough to bring hold-up horses into the race late and Superior Choice ties up inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If Ragazzo Grandi travels prominently or makes a forward move and proves significantly better than the bare form of this field suggests.
scenarios.body: If Ragazzo Grandi travels prominently or makes a forward move and proves significantly better than the bare form of this field suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Collars Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Hatteen, repositioned in midfield, travels smoothly and picks up strongly having been close enough to the pace.
scenarios.body: If Hatteen, repositioned in midfield, travels smoothly and picks up strongly having been close enough to the pace.

watchPoints.text: Superior Choice — if it jumps cleanly and secures the lead unchallenged within the first furlong, the race shape is set and the hold-up horses face a structural trap for the remainder of the mile-and-two.
Ragazzo Grandi — watch its early behaviour and where George Wood positions it; if it slots prominently behind Superior Choice, its unknown ceiling becomes a live danger to the favourite.

Act Of Generosity — Zac Lloyd will need to make a decision early whether to commit or wait; if he waits and the pace is modest, the hold-up strategy could leave Varian's runner with too much ground to make up entering the Newmarket straight.

Hatteen — Rob Hornby's instructions will be telling; if Hatteen is held back to its natural position at the rear in a field of five with a moderate pace, it will face a very long run from last to first on the home straight at Newmarket.
Zurna — 11 days between runs is tight; monitor her going to post for any signs of freshness or flat work that might indicate whether the quick return is a sign of confidence or necessity.

races.name: Zyn Pole Position Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Madame De Sevigne
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with patchy recent form including a fair 3rd at Sandown on Standard ground; Newmarket 7f Good is a new test and her sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 attempts on turf is a significant negative flag.

runners_data.name: Bravo Zulu
runners_data.note: Two wins and four places on similar going give her the best conversion rate among the hold-up brigade; stepping back to 7f after recent 6f runs may suit, though Laura Pearson's claim is the key rider angle to monitor.

runners_data.name: Stenmark
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two places from three starts at 7f on Good — the trip and going combination is his sweet spot; William Carson rides for a yard with zero wins in 14 days, but the horse's own form profile is well-suited to this shape.

runners_data.name: Potomac River
runners_data.note: Holds a 7f Good win in his recent form string and is genuinely a hold-up type in practice, though the crowded closing group means he may not get his preferred passage; discount his chance slightly given he cannot secure his natural position in this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cobbler
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip and going combination last time out, which is the standout positive; his natural style is to close from off the pace, but with many rivals doing the same he may find himself boxed in rather than finding clear daylight through the dip.

runners_data.name: Dashing Dick
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who prefers closing from the rear, but his recent string of 6f runs on Good going produced three finishes of 7th or worse — the step up to 7f helps, yet his out-of-role mapping compounds existing form concerns.

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: Returned from a 54-day break and has shown ability at 7f on Good in his history, though he is a hold-up type shuffled forward on the map; Harry Vigors's 7lb claim is the main value argument, but the layoff and crowded closing group are genuine risks.

runners_data.name: Gallant
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and top weight at 137lbs; his Newmarket form over shorter trips has been modest (no wins or places on similar going in 13 attempts), but the uncontested lead at 7f is a significant positional upgrade and the key variable in this race.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: Has been placed at 7f on Good twice from six attempts and showed speed when runner-up recently; Rob Hornby's booking for a yard with just one win from 14-day records is noted, and only 8 days since last run means freshness is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good going and possesses course form, but his recent record of five starts without a win on Good turf (including a 16th last time at Newmarket) tempers enthusiasm significantly; J F Egan's booking adds professional weight to his claims.

races.paceDynamic: Gallant is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful rival pressing for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over Newmarket's July course 7f. Stenmark and Miletus will push forward to sit just behind, creating a small prominent group, but with Gallant uncontested this is unlikely to be a truly searching pace — more a steady-to-moderate tempo that keeps the race together until the final two furlongs. The field contains more hold-up horses than the shape can genuinely accommodate: Potomac River, Cherry Cobbler, Dashing Dick, and Eazy On The Eye are all redistributed to midfield on the map but are true hold-up types unlikely to secure their natural rear position in a race with this many closers. A controlled front-running pace over 7f on Good turf at Newmarket typically sets up a pronounced advantage for horses who can track the pace prominently and sustain their effort through the dip — prominent racers sitting just off Gallant are the primary beneficiaries here, while genuine hold-up horses face a field too congested at the back and a pace too moderate to produce a dramatic late surge.

scenarios.body: If Gallant leads comfortably at a steady-to-moderate tempo and the race is decided by sustained galloping in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.body: If the tempo quickens sharply in the middle stages, stringing the field out and giving hold-up horses a genuine run at those who have led.

scenarios.body: If the pace remains so slow that Gallant is never headed and simply outstays rivals on the long Newmarket straight.

watchPoints.text: Gallant (front-runner) sets the entire pace shape — if he finds cover quickly and dictates unchallenged, prominent horses Stenmark and Miletus receive a significant tactical advantage and the hold-up group faces a wall of traffic.

Cherry Cobbler and Potomac River are both genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map — watch the early stages to see whether the jockeys attempt to push forward or accept their position, as this will determine whether any late finish is viable.
Eazy On The Eye returns from a 54-day absence for Heather Main, whose yard has not fired recently; an unraced horse in a compact closing group is a significant price risk if fitness is not spot-on.

Bravo Zulu has two wins on similar going and is the most credentialed hold-up horse in the field — if the pace quickens enough to string the field out in the straight, she is the most likely beneficiary of a late rush.

Dashing Dick's three consecutive 7th-or-worse finishes over 6f on Good should be watched as a pace-stamina indicator — if he finishes closer, it signals the pace was slower than anticipated and front-end horses benefited throughout.

races.name: Zyn Pole Position Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Physique
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Micky Fenton and Grace McEntee who needs things to happen in front of her; similar-going form reads 0W3P in 10 runs which is a concern for winning prospects, though she stays seven furlongs well and is 20 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Benacre
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's six-year-old has a solid recent record of placing at this trip on Good ground (2nd and 3rd in last five here), sits prominently for Jack Callan and is likely to be among those pressing Al Karrar — consistency without a win in a long time is the worry.

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Joey Haynes rides this hold-up performer who carries a hood and has shown two wins at this distance on Good-equivalent going in recent history; 22 days since last run is straightforward but the stable's modest 14-day strike rate (0/3) tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Drifts Away
runners_data.note: Lightly raced this season after a 295-day absence, which is a significant flag, but won at 7f on Soft and placed prominently in the past; George Wood takes the ride and the horse typically sits in a handy position though the long layoff makes fitness a genuine question mark.

runners_data.name: Great Mates
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose natural role is tracking the pace, but with Al Karrar, Best Rate, and Benacre all ahead of him in the queue, Daniel Tudhope will find him pushed wider and further back than ideal; the horse's best form has come at 8f on Tapeta so the turf drop and shorter trip compound the positional issue.

runners_data.name: Noble Guest
runners_data.note: Zac Lloyd partners this true hold-up performer who has shown ability on Good ground (1W3P in 9 runs), but the redistribution note means he is likely to find himself in midfield rather than at the rear where he switches off best — his closing kick may be blunted by having to race in an unnatural comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Al Karrar
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's six-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and Dougie Costello should get him rolling from the front unchallenged; the horse's best form has come at 6f so stamina over seven furlongs is a legitimate query, and his OR of 82 tops the field, but the style_fit tag reflects that this 7f Good trip is a step into slightly less certain territory.

runners_data.name: Best Rate
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old was out just eight days ago, is lightly weighted relative to ability, and sits prominently under Alec Voikhansky; the form string of 4-4643 shows consistent placing without winning and his 3/15 record on similar going is modest, but he is likely to be the horse most immediately dangerous to Al Karrar as the race develops.

runners_data.name: Longlai
runners_data.note: George Baker's eight-year-old hasn't run since last September (226-day absence) and that fitness concern is the dominant factor; a hold-up performer at 7f on Good ground who has placed once in similar conditions, but the layoff makes it hard to trust him until he shows he retains his ability.

races.paceDynamic: Al Karrar is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to match him for the early lead, he should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, honest gallop over this seven-furlong Newmarket July Course trip on Good ground. Best Rate and Benacre are the most likely prominent chasers to sit just behind him, meaning the tempo will be set by Al Karrar but not truly pressured into something unsustainably fast. This field carries more prominent pace than the map can accommodate: Great Mates is a genuine prominent type who will find himself racing further back than ideal, and Noble Guest is a true hold-up horse similarly out of position — neither is likely to secure their natural role in this shape. With a single pace-setter controlling a steady-to-fair gallop and the race unlikely to produce a true test of stamina, horses capable of travelling prominently and sustaining their effort into the Dip will be best placed, giving a clear edge to those sitting second or third and able to pounce when Al Karrar's advantage is eroded.

scenarios.body: If Al Karrar bowls along uncontested and the pace is steady enough to favour those tracking closely.

scenarios.body: If the gallop is genuine enough to string the field out and the horses immediately tracking Al Karrar produce a sustained challenge from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If Al Karrar goes too fast too soon and the pace collapses inside the final two furlongs, leaving the field to come back to the closers.
scenarios.body: If Al Karrar goes too fast too soon and the pace collapses inside the final two furlongs, leaving the field to come back to the closers.

scenarios.trigger: If Al Karrar is slowly away or checked early, removing the pacemaker and producing a ragged, falsely-run contest.
scenarios.body: If Al Karrar is slowly away or checked early, removing the pacemaker and producing a ragged, falsely-run contest.

watchPoints.text: Al Karrar's stamina over 7f is the pivotal factor — if he ties up inside the final furlong after controlling the pace, Best Rate and Benacre who are tracking him most closely will benefit most directly.

Drifts Away returns from 295 days off and if fitness is not fully there, a prominent position early could see him fade sharply and interfere with others in the straight — monitor market moves as a fitness barometer.

Great Mates and Noble Guest are both likely to find themselves racing out of their natural positions; if the race is run at a pace that suits their preferred style they could outrun their odds, but both should be treated with caution in any scenario requiring them to perform from an unfamiliar position.

The Good ground is consistent across all July Course races today, meaning no surface variability to factor in — times from earlier races (particularly the 5:55 over the same 7f trip) should be used as a benchmark to judge whether Al Karrar set a genuinely honest gallop.

Benacre's jockey Jack Callan claims 3lb, reducing his burden to 128lbs effectively — in a field where margins will be tight, that weight relief could be the difference if he and Best Rate finish in a cluster behind the leader.

races.name: Zyn Frontrunner Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Hard To Believe
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo showed a win over this trip on Tapeta and another over 10f on Stardust, but both good-ground runs have disappointed (6th, 7th) and the sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places on similar ground is a genuine flag despite the prominent racing style suiting this shape.

runners_data.name: Outback Legend
runners_data.note: The clear pace-setter here, winning last time over 12f on Soft gives trip confidence, but both Good-ground runs have been moderate (3rd and 6th at 10f) and a STYLE_FIT tag of 0.90 reflects that this uncontested front-running role is actually outside its normal pattern — the lone lead is his to take, yet that Good-ground form tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed & Jose Santos's 3yo is a natural front-runner by inclination whose best effort was a second over 8f on Good, but with multiple pace types in the field he is likely to be shuffled off his ideal berth; the STYLE_FIT discount applies given the crowded prominent group, and his form at 7-8f on similar ground (mixed) raises a question over the extra distance.

runners_data.name: Temple
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's hold-up 3yo has 55 days between runs and a light recent record, but the third over 8f on Soft shows ability to stay and the pure closer profile is naturally suited to sitting off a Outback Legend-controlled pace — Sorin Moldoveanu's 7lb claim helps on the weights.

runners_data.name: Outflank
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's consistent 3yo has placed in all three career starts (three thirds) over distances from 10f to 12f, the Good-ground run at 12f was a placed effort, and the Unknown style tag means tactical options are open; the blinkered headgear is noted and Luke Catton's 3lb claim is a practical advantage over the weights.

runners_data.name: Battosai
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's 3yo returns on a 14-day turnaround, wears a hood, and has raced six times on Good ground without winning — the sim-going record of 0W/1P from six Good runs is the most exposed profile in the field; though a natural prominent type by instinct, the redistribution means he is unlikely to secure that position here, limiting his scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Outback Legend is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter across 1m4f on Good ground at Newmarket's July course, this race will almost certainly be run at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front. Outback Legend shapes to dictate through a measured early gallop, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead, which means fractions are unlikely to be punishing and the front two furlongs will be covered at a relaxed clip. The field holds more prominent-type horses than can realistically get their natural position — Brave Hunter and Battosai are both genuine prominent types but are effectively displaced into midfield given Outback Legend's role, meaning they will either have to be restrained or burn stamina pressing forward. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a honest-but-not-brutal pace — strongly favours horses with proven stamina who can travel smoothly in a compact pack and accelerate off an honest but unhurried gallop, making patient hold-up or midfield-to-prominent profiles best placed, with Outflank's consistent placing profile and Temple's staying potential both interesting.

scenarios.title: Outback Legend Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Outback Legend bowls along uncontested and dictates a steady-to-honest pace throughout.
scenarios.body: If Outback Legend bowls along uncontested and dictates a steady-to-honest pace throughout.

scenarios.title: Prominent Types Crowd Front

scenarios.body: If Brave Hunter or Battosai push up despite redistribution and force a contested pace.

scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If Outback Legend crawls and the pace is so slow it sets up a sprint finish over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Outback Legend crawls and the pace is so slow it sets up a sprint finish over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Outback Legend fades sharply in the closing stages and backmarkers swoop late.
scenarios.body: If Outback Legend fades sharply in the closing stages and backmarkers swoop late.

watchPoints.text: Outback Legend — watch whether it jumps cleanly and immediately goes to the front; if another runner disputes the lead early, the whole pace dynamic shifts from solo control to a contested scenario that changes every probability.

Brave Hunter and Battosai — both natural prominent types; if either pushes hard for position in the first half mile despite the redistribution tag, early fractions will increase sharply and Outflank or Temple's patient profiles benefit most.

Outflank — three consecutive thirds suggest a horse on the cusp of a win; watch whether Luke Catton uses the claim aggressively to position closer than the Unknown style tag implies, which would suit Scenario A strongly.

Temple — 55 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field; watch the market move to gauge Chapple-Hyam's confidence that the horse is ready to run to its best given the limited recent evidence.

Going — all races on the Newmarket July card today are confirmed Good; no material deterioration expected, so no runner faces an unexpected going concern, but watch for any ground updates closer to post given the number of horses whose form profile is untested on genuine Good.

races.name: Zyn Frontrunner Finish Handicap

runners_data.name: Spell Master
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who goes well fresh (won 13 days ago), handles Good ground and 7f-1m well, trainer Oli Rix in quiet form at 1/5 over 14 days, but Jonny Peate's claim makes the weight workable; shapes to press Fort Rock for the secondary position.

runners_data.name: Exposure
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden runner returning from 249 days off, so fitness is the obvious query; genuinely wants to race prominently but the packed early positions mean he is likely to find himself further back than preferred, softening his chance considerably.

runners_data.name: Stem
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon yard in good nick at 6/57 over 14 days and Alec Voikhansky takes the ride, but on similar Good ground Stem has managed only 2 wins from 7 and his last two runs were well beaten; a true front-runner by nature, he is squeezed out of his preferred spot here by the glut of pace in this field.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for George Margarson, apprentice Olivia Haines claims 7lb, but the flat pace this race is likely to set is the concern — on Good-ish ground over the past 15 runs he has placed 4 times without winning, and needs a stronger gallop than Spanish Voice will likely provide.

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Ed Walker runner who is naturally prominent but cannot get that position here; has won and placed on similar ground in a 7f-sprint context, but stepping to a mile in a field with excess pace types is an awkward ask for his style.

runners_data.name: Fort Rock
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's lightly-raced three-year-old has won twice at 7f on Tapeta then finished third on Good ground over a mile — the step up in trip and straight Bunbury course suit, and his OR of 90 off low mileage makes him a primary beneficiary of the prominent profile.

runners_data.name: Synners Kid
runners_data.note: Henry Dwyer's three-year-old won twice in soft ground and has been held up in his last two on Good — neither prominent nor hold-up enough to be definitive, and consistent Good-ground form is absent (0 wins, 0 places from 5 on similar ground).

runners_data.name: Elan d'Or
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams runner who genuinely wants to be up with the pace, having won twice on Tapeta and placed from the front; squeezed into midfield by the weight of prominent horses in this race, he needs everything to go wrong for rivals to reclaim his natural position.

runners_data.name: Loz Vegas
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who won over a mile on Good; needs a faster pace than Spanish Voice is likely to set to get competitive, though Good ground at this trip is not a problem.

runners_data.name: Magnatura
runners_data.note: Tom Ward runner who has won twice, most recently on Good over 7f, and appreciates forcing tactics; pushed out of that role here by the volume of pace in the field, a midfield position blunts his best form profile significantly.

runners_data.name: Ramli
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — disregard for race-shape purposes.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's seven-year-old is a confirmed hold-up horse, won on Good ground over a mile last time, and Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a small bonus; his 1W5P record over 15 similar-going runs shows he is competitively placed when conditions suit, but needs a genuine pace to close into.

runners_data.name: Spanish Voice
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here — Andrew Balding's in-form yard (12/65 over 14 days), two Good-ground wins from seven similar runs, and tongue-tie retained; with no credible pace rival, he controls the tempo and is the axis around which the entire race shape is built.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon prominent runner who has won over a mile on Tapeta and performed around this distance on Good; blinkered, which suggests keenness, and could push for a forward berth alongside Fort Rock, but six-runner losing run is a caution.

runners_data.name: Release The Storm
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's four-year-old has won his last two on Good ground over 7f, progressive, and Harry Vigors claims 7lb; a natural prominently-positioned horse who should find a forward pitch without the pressure that redistribution causes, making him a legitimate beneficiary of the controlled pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Dark Tornado
runners_data.note: J F Egan rides this Michael Wigham hold-up horse who has won twice on Good ground from 11 Good-ground runs and wears a visor; genuine closer, but Spanish Voice's likely slow tempo is the problem — he has placed 5 times but needs pace to collapse in front.

races.paceDynamic: Spanish Voice is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a largely uncontested lead on offer, shapes to control this race from the front at a sustainable gallop around the Bunbury Mile. Fort Rock, Spell Master, Synners Kid, Angel Hunter, and Release The Storm are the prominent types most likely to actually lock in positions just off the pace, while Elan d'Or, Exposure, Stem, Arctic Thunder, Magnatura, and Ramli are genuine prominent/front-running horses who cannot all get their natural pitch in a 16-runner field and will find themselves racing further back than ideal. With Spanish Voice dictating an uncontested, measured tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently in the first half-dozen — pressing or tracking the leader — and quicken from a handy position, as genuine hold-up horses will need a stronger pace than Spanish Voice is likely to set to generate a meaningful late run. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate, and those most likely to actually secure a forward berth are Fort Rock, Spell Master, and Release The Storm, given their profiles, yards, and recent form.

watchPoints.text: Spanish Voice is the pace anchor — watch whether Callum Hutchinson sends him forward immediately or allows a stride of hesitation, as any slow break risks Fort Rock or Release The Storm stealing the rail and the lead.

Fort Rock (Charlie Appleby, lightly-raced, OR=90) maps prominently on limited form — if he travels strongly into the race from a handy position he could strike before rivals know it, and his handicap mark may underestimate him.

Release The Storm has won his last two on Good ground and Harry Vigors's 7lb claim brings him into weight contention — watch whether Meehan instructs aggressive early tactics to use the strong recent form before rivals settle.

Sterling Knight and Dark Tornado are the hold-up horses most likely to make it competitive if the pace quickens at all — both hold strong Good-ground records over the mile and their finishing runs will signal whether the pace was genuine enough to bring the back of the field into play.

The cluster of redistributed prominent horses (Elan d'Or, Exposure, Stem, Arctic Thunder, Magnatura) will all be forced wider or further back than they want — monitor early traffic to see if any force their way forward, as that would materially alter the race's pace structure.

races.name: Zyn Strong Stride Handicap

runners_data.name: Phantom Watch
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with visor (blinkers/visor noted), trained by Hugo Palmer who has been active lately; 140 days off is a notable absence, but has placed twice at 8f on Tapeta-equivalent good ground and should be suited by the mile if the pace is strong enough to set up a late run.

runners_data.name: Crimson Rambler
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Tapeta in good conditions and placed twice in similar company; genuine hold-up horse whose natural style is towards the rear, though the redistribution flags he may need to race more prominently than ideal in this field — the blinkered headgear suggests a tactical shift is possible and Liam Wright's 5lb claim is a bonus.

runners_data.name: Mimi's Magic
runners_data.note: Unknown-style runner for Ed Dunlop, who has had two winners from 18 in the past fortnight; placed at a mile on Good and at 10f on Tapeta, suggesting genuine stamina for the trip — Jack Callan's 3lb claim could be a small edge in what looks a tight handicap.

runners_data.name: Jamie Sommers
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at the mile on Good ground under Laura Pearson, with three placed efforts in her last five at the trip; a natural hold-up horse who will likely find herself racing in advance of her preferred position in this shape, which may blunt her finishing kick at the business end.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Laughter
runners_data.note: Unproven style runner for Ed Walker who is in good recent form (6/40 in 14 days); 205 days off the track is a serious fitness concern and form over 7f on various going types leaves stamina for a mile unproven — only one run on Good ground in the recent history.

runners_data.name: Malika
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up filly has only three runs to assess and showed a placed effort over 10f on Good, suggesting the mile may even be short of her optimum; the redistribution means she will race closer than natural, and with a STYLE_FIT discount applied her chance in this shape is tempered.

runners_data.name: Guest House
runners_data.note: Best form pointer is a win at 8f on Good for George Margarson, and she has six runs on the going with a win and two places — solid course-going profile; true hold-up horse who will be shuffled forward out of position, but J F Egan is an astute jockey who may find a way to manage the compromise.

runners_data.name: Crafty Blue
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Tapeta for Richard Hannon but his two subsequent 8f runs on Tapeta and Soft produced finishing positions of 9 and 9 — no evidence he stays the mile or handles Good ground; 44-day absence and the highest OR in the field at 70 means he is weighted to the teeth.

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Has placed at 8f on Good and 10f on Tapeta, and beaten only three on his most recent start; Michael Bell in fair recent form, 13 days since last run, and his hold-up profile means he will need a strong pace to deliver — the Good ground and mile trip suit on form.

runners_data.name: Safe Harbor
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and the key pace ingredient; Marco Botti's filly has placed twice on Good at 8f and sets the tactical agenda for the entire race — the STYLE_FIT flag reflects she is a prominent rather than confirmed leader, but no rival is likely to take the role from her.

races.paceDynamic: Safe Harbor is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to dispute the lead, Jack Gilligan can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits on Good ground over a mile at Newmarket's July course. The field is unusually hold-up heavy — Phantom Watch, Crafty Blue, Royal Bodyguard, and several redistributed types will all be tracking from off the pace — but none of them carry the early speed to meaningfully pressure Safe Harbor through the first half. Crimson Rambler, Jamie Sommers, Malika, and Guest House are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; of these, Guest House and Crimson Rambler are most likely to physically get closest to a prominent pitch given their recent form patterns and tactical flexibility. With a single uncontested pacesetter controlling a modest, honest gallop on a flat, fair track, this race shape most favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can track the pace and produce a sustained finish — pure deep closers will find the tempo insufficient to produce their best late charge.

scenarios.title: Safe Harbor Controls, Rail Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Safe Harbor bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable, even gallop that suits horses finishing off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Safe Harbor bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable, even gallop that suits horses finishing off the pace.

scenarios.trigger: If Safe Harbor's lead turns into a crawl through the middle and several hold-up horses find themselves trapped out of position.
scenarios.body: If Safe Harbor's lead turns into a crawl through the middle and several hold-up horses find themselves trapped out of position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If a mid-division horse travels smoothly in the slipstream and produces a decisive turn of foot in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: If a mid-division horse travels smoothly in the slipstream and produces a decisive turn of foot in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Front Two Last
scenarios.trigger: If Safe Harbor is pressured earlier than expected or finds the second half of the trip beyond her, gifting a winning lead to a prominent challenger.
scenarios.body: If Safe Harbor is pressured earlier than expected or finds the second half of the trip beyond her, gifting a winning lead to a prominent challenger.

watchPoints.text: Safe Harbor's early position is the fulcrum of the entire race — if Jack Gilligan is forced wider than stall position allows or is pressured in the first furlong by a keen hold-up horse jumping fast, the anticipated controlled pace evaporates and every scenario probability shifts.

Crimson Rambler and Guest House are the two redistributed hold-up horses most likely to physically end up closer to the pace than their natural style demands — watch how they jump and whether Liam Wright or J F Egan attempt to secure cover early, as a traffic-scramble between these two could compromise both.

Hurricane Laughter has been off 205 days and has no established mile form; if Ed Walker has targeted this specific race for a fitness run rather than a win, the horse could either set a falsely generous gallop by bowling forward or, if prominent, compound and interfere with finishing positions behind.

Phantom Watch's 140-day absence and hold-up style mean Daniel Tudhope will need a strongly run race and a clean passage — if the field compresses through the final three furlongs, Phantom Watch is most vulnerable to being squeezed out of a winning run despite possessing the profile to finish well.

races.name: Find Your Zyn Moment Handicap

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with Good ground form (1/6f/GOO last time) and an OR of 73 at the top of the weights; Ruth Carr's horse has a strong recent record in this role but the STYLE_FIT flag reminds us she is being asked to lead in a race where the map places her prominently — her chance depends entirely on executing uncontested.

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at 4 years old, trainer Adam Kirby in excellent 14-day form (1/13); predominantly a 5f horse stepping up to 6f on Good ground with limited evidence at this trip, which is a genuine concern despite a course win in his record.

runners_data.name: Spring Bloom
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up specialist with solid place form on Good ground (11/15 sim-going) and Callum Hutchinson aboard; dropping from 5f where recent form sits means the extra furlong here suits her natural style, though her age and modest OR limit ceiling.

runners_data.name: Rebel Path
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams yard is out of form (0/21 T14) and Olivia Haines claims 7lbs from a low base; the horse holds Good-ground wins but the 34-day gap and trainer form are both against, and from a true hold-up draw there is a real risk of getting nowhere in traffic.

runners_data.name: State Of Madness
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from Mark Loughnane's yard which is also out of current form (0/21 T14); Good-ground profile is thin (2/15 sim-going) and having been beaten a long way in recent starts, his chance relies on the prominent position working in his favour rather than any recent trend.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Knocker
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who won over 6f on Soft last time out but is only 0W/1P in four Good-ground attempts (4/13 sim-going); the headgear note (t) and 25-day freshener could help, but the going profile is a genuine question mark.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jenny
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's yard is in form (3/14 T14) and Spirit Of Jenny has four placed efforts from five Good-ground runs (5/9 sim-going); tracks the pace naturally at 6f and the lack of a win recently is offset by consistent placed form and a positive trainer pattern.

runners_data.name: Ancient Times
runners_data.note: 197 days off the track is a severe concern for an 8-year-old; headgear (t) could sharpen focus but the form string of 30600 is poor, and despite a good sim-going record historically (8/15, 2W4P), this is a big ask first time back.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Warrior
runners_data.note: Won twice on Standard last season and returns after 119 days; headgear (p) worn previously and the sim-going record is modest (4/15), suggesting Good turf may not be the surface this horse wants — a wide draw in an 18-runner sprint makes the task harder.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Ross Burdon is in fine form (2/3 T14) and this horse won last time over 7f on Good; a true hold-up operator whose note carries the honest caveat that this field is packed with closers, meaning Northcliff will be squeezed into a deeper position than ideal and needs the race to pan out perfectly.

runners_data.name: Havana Sky
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's 5-year-old has recorded four placed efforts across varying trips but recent form has dried up (2-0844); operates as a genuine hold-up type who, with the race's closer congestion, will need a seam of daylight that may not appear in an 18-runner 6f heat.

runners_data.name: Way To Dubai
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby horses are showing form (3/22 T14) but Way To Dubai is 52 days off the track with zero wins or places in Good-ground runs (0W0P sim-going); naturally sits at the rear and finds himself in a midfield map position because closers outnumber the space available — a poor tactical slot.

runners_data.name: Currahee
runners_data.note: 283 days off the track is a major negative for this 4-year-old who won at 6f on Good previously; a natural closer who has been remapped to midfield given closer congestion, so his reappearance chance depends on fitness and the race opening up — both uncertain.

runners_data.name: Clasina
runners_data.note: Long absence (299 days) is the dominant story here, stepping back from 7f to 6f; despite a Good-ground record of 10/15 sim-going with a win, the combination of the layoff, a natural hold-up style squeezed into an awkward midfield position, and OR of 62 makes this a very hard race to win.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Blinkers (b) applied by Conrad Allen and has been placed in three of last four starts; prominent racer who is nicely fresh (9 days) and has the kind of consistent placed form at 6f on Good that makes him a legitimate each-way player in the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha yard in form (2/29 T14) but Mart has only one run on similar going (1/15 sim-going) and no wins from 15 Good-turf starts; a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield berth by sheer weight of closers in the draw, limiting late impact.

runners_data.name: Grand Citadel
runners_data.note: Micky Fenton's lowly ranked runner carries blinkers (b) and has won at 7f on Good and placed at 6f; a front-running type who has been stepping down in trip with improving form (945321), and the 25-day gap is fine — the 6f on Good turf suits the profile better than connections' recent pattern might suggest.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sorbet
runners_data.note: Jim & Suzi Best's 4-year-old has limited evidence (4 runs) and modest sim-going form (2/4); Olivia Tubb claims 5lbs but this is a genuine long-shot hold-up horse, relocated into midfield on the map, facing an 18-runner sprint with no obvious angle.

races.paceDynamic: Fiscal Policy is the one confirmed front-runner here and, critically, faces minimal pressure to burn early — with no other genuine pace horse to challenge her for the lead, she should be able to stride into a sustainable rhythm on Good ground at the July Course. Ancient State, Spirit Of Jenny, State Of Madness, and Elvetham are the principal prominent types who will look to track her in the first two furlongs, creating a mid-tempo scenario rather than a scorching gallop. The field is genuinely saturated with natural hold-up horses — Northcliff, Havana Sky, Way To Dubai, Currahee, Clasina, Mart, and Rainbow Sorbet are all true closers who cannot all find their preferred rearward berth and will be bunched in mid-to-rear division; of these, Northcliff and Way To Dubai on Good ground carry the strongest claims to carve out a run late if room materialises. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner on a flat, fair track — firmly favours horses racing prominently in second or third who can conserve energy early and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than genuine closers who will face traffic and a compressed finish.

watchPoints.text: Fiscal Policy — if she is bumped or checked leaving the stalls she loses her uncontested lead, which is the central assumption underpinning the most likely race shape; watch the break.

Spirit Of Jenny — Steph Hollinshead yard in sharp form and this horse's sim-going placing record (4/9) is notably strong; if she tracks Fiscal Policy smoothly she becomes the chief threat to the leader without needing anything to go wrong for rivals.

Northcliff — Rob Hornby rides for Ross Burdon who has a 2/3 T14 strike-rate, and the horse won last time on Good over 7f; the redistribution into mid-pack is a genuine positional disadvantage, but if the pace compresses and he finds a gap from 2f out he could land a blow.

Ancient State — stepping from 5f to 6f for the first time on Good turf; if stamina does not hold it may drop away sharply in the closing stages and open the door for hold-up horses who have been squeezed wide.
Elvetham — blinkers freshly applied and a 9-day turnaround with three consecutive placed efforts; a quietly improving handicapper who could outrun a larger price if the prominent group dominates.
